package_info.why_malicious: The package is a trojanized version of the legitimate discord.js library, containing obfuscated code that steals Discord tokens from local storage and exfiltrates them to an attacker-controlled server.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code iterates over browser and Discord client local storage folders, searches for Discord tokens using regex, and exfiltrates any found tokens along with the victim's IP address to a hardcoded remote server via HTTP POST.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing browser and Discord client storage to extract tokens is not expected in a legitimate library. Exfiltrating these tokens to an external server is a clear sign of credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate discord.js library should not access local storage folders or transmit sensitive tokens externally.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate software may access local storage for user settings, but never for credential exfiltration.
key_indicators: Obfuscated code injected into a core library file
Regex searching for Discord token patterns
Network POST to hardcoded attacker-controlled domain
Enumeration of multiple browser/Discord storage paths

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code exfiltrates stolen Discord tokens to a hardcoded Discord webhook endpoint via HTTP POST.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Sending sensitive tokens to a Discord webhook is a common exfiltration method for malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not transmit user credentials to external webhooks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Webhooks are used for automation, but never for credential exfiltration.
key_indicators: POST request containing sensitive token data

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code injects malicious JavaScript into the Discord client, steals sensitive user data (credentials, credit cards, PII), and sends it to a hardcoded webhook.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Injecting code into another application's process and exfiltrating sensitive data is a hallmark of infostealer malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not modify or inject code into other applications, nor steal and transmit user data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; code injection and credential theft are never legitimate.
key_indicators: Exfiltration of PII and credentials to webhook

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// List of commands:
!webcampic - Takes a picture from the webcam
!screenshot - Takes the screenshot of the user's current screen
!vbs - Executes VBScript code received from the attacker
!Powershell - Executes PowerShell code received from the attacker
!clipboard - sends to the attacker content of the clipboard
!download - downloads file from the victim machine
!geolocated - send data from https://geolocation-db.com/json/
!passwords - sends to the attacker all passwords stored in a system
!shell - execute a shell command
!tokens - send to the attacker discord tokens
!listprocess - receive information about running processes
!startup - add a file to the startup
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code listens for attacker commands via Discord chat and executes a wide range of remote access and data theft actions, including webcam capture, screenshot, shell execution, credential theft, and persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote access trojans (RATs) providing full control to an attacker are highly malicious, especially when obfuscated and distributed as npm packages.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should provide remote shell, webcam, or credential theft capabilities.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote administration tools exist, but not in the context of npm packages or without user consent.

execution_context.file_location: main package file (wafer-* family, octavius-public, mrg-message-broker)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code collects all environment variables from the process and exfiltrates them as a base64-encoded string to a hardcoded external server via HTTP POST.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Stealing environment variables is a common method for harvesting secrets (API keys, credentials) from developer and CI/CD environments.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not exfiltrate environment variables to external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or crash reporting may send limited environment info, but never full environment variables.

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the malicious npm package, often via typosquatting or dependency confusion.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is executed in the context of the victim's environment.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes at import-time or runtime, harvesting sensitive data (Discord tokens, environment variables, credentials, PII).
Stolen data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure (custom servers, Discord webhooks, pipedream.net endpoints).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive data, enabling account takeover, further attacks, or resale.

attack_chain.action: In the case of RATs, attacker may issue further commands for remote control, persistence, or lateral movement.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of the victim system.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated code in npm packages, especially in core library files
Access to browser or Discord client local storage folders
Network requests to hardcoded external domains or Discord webhooks
Exfiltration of environment variables or credentials
Presence of remote access or shell execution commands
file_indicators: References to Discord client storage paths
Obfuscated code blocks in wafer-* or similar packages
network_indicators: Unusual outbound traffic to domains not associated with legitimate package functionality
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages containing obfuscated code, especially in files that should not contain such logic (e.g., core library files). Flag packages that access browser or Discord client storage, search for Discord token regex patterns, or exfiltrate data to hardcoded domains/webhooks. Detect base64-encoded environment variable exfiltration and the presence of remote access command handlers. Use network monitoring to identify suspicious outbound POST requests to known exfiltration endpoints.
